topic: The Life and Achievements of Filippo Brunelleschi
passage: Filippo Brunelleschi considers to be the founding father of Renaissance architecture.
He was born in Florence in 1377.
Filippo was artistically talented, and trained as a goldsmith and a clockmaker before becoming an architecture.
When he was around 25, he traveled to Rome with his friend, the sculptor Donatello, who he studied the remains of ancient Roman buildings.
His first architectural commission was the Ospedale degli Innocenti, that is one of the great Renaissance building.
A number of other fine works, including chapels in Florentine churches, strengthening his reputation.
And the stunning dome of Il Duomo is his masterpiece.
He also designed machinery to produce special effects in theatrical productions.
He died in Florence and buried in Il Duomo.
